title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 7 Secundo: foresight of perseverance concurrent — not prior cause of predestination
pass_a_gloss: Second: what the adversaries say — that God predestines no one to the crown except whom he foresees will persevere — is to be admitted as true insofar as it posits that the same singular persons who are predestined to glory are at the same time foreseen by God as going to persevere in grace. But insofar as it supposes this foresight to be the cause of predestination, and prior to it according to our way of understanding, it is altogether to be rejected.
pass_b_english: Second: when opponents say God predestines to the crown only those he foresees will persevere, grant it this far — the same people predestined to glory are also foreseen as going to persevere in grace. Reject it when they make that foresight the cause of predestination, and prior to it in our order of thought.
source_text: Secundo, quod dicunt adversarii, Deum neminem praedestinare ad coronam nisi quem praevidet perseveraturum, eatenus pro vero admittendum, quatenus ponit easdem singulares personas quae praedestinantur ad gloriam, esse praevisas simul a Deo ut perseveraturas in gratia. Sed quatenus supponit hanc praevisionem esse causam praedestinationis, & secundum nostrum modum intelligendi illa priorem, est omnino repudiandum.
